title: Delegated rotation and retention for scoped API keys
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Current token governance requires operator/admin intervention for most rotations and long-term retention is manual. Customers and infra teams want per-scope keys that can be rotated automatically by delegated agents (service accounts, platform tooling) while preserving auditability and safe retention/escrow for incident forensics. This ticket implements a delegated rotation API and retention/escrow policy for scoped API keys, tightly integrated with RBAC v2 and audit logging.

Goals:
- Allow non-admin principals (service accounts, platform workers) to rotate keys they own or manage, if granted a narrow 'credential_steward' role on the key scope.
- Introduce a rotation delegation token: short-lived, single-use credential that authorizes a rotation operation for a single key scope.
- Enforce naming and metadata templates for all new keys to improve discoverability (env.scope.owner.createdAt.rotationEpoch).
- Implement an escrow/retention store for old key material: archived encrypted blobs with 90-day retention by default and automatic purge after retention window.
- Record structured audit events for every rotation, expiry, revoke, and escrow retrieval with correlation_id for tracing.
- Provide emergency mass-revoke and cross-region propagation path for Hosted and Dedicated; document Private deployment differences (KMS integration required).

Design summary:
1) Authorization: RBAC v2 adds two new privileges: credential_steward (can request rotation for keys in scope) and credential_admin (full lifecycle). Roles map to roots and teams in the existing RBAC hierarchy. Rotation delegation is a scoped grant that can be timeboxed.
2) Rotation API: POST /v1/keys/{key_id}/rotate with optional parameter 'delegation_token'. If called without a token, caller must have credential_admin on the key. If called with token, backend validates token signature and scope claims. Response returns new key_id, new key metadata, and rotation epoch.
3) Delegation token workflow: Admins create delegation tokens scoped to one scope/id and TTL via UI/API. Tokens are single use and recorded in audit logs when minted and when consumed. Tokens can be minted by credential_admins or by automation with high-assurance flows (signed requests from orchestration cluster).
4) Escrow and retention: When a key is rotated, old key material is encrypted with a KMS-wrapped data key and stored in the escrow bucket tagged with reason, key_id, owner, created_at, rotation_epoch and correlation_id. Default retention 90 days; retention configurable per-org (0-365). Retrieval requires credential_admin plus explicit audit justification and generates an audit event to S3/BigQuery. Keys beyond retention are deleted irreversibly.
5) Naming and metadata enforcement: New key creation enforces a naming template and requires metadata fields: owner (user/service), scope, environment, purpose, and compliance tags. Existing keys will be migrated in a best-effort fashion using a background job that annotates name/metadata where possible and surfaces exceptions to admins.
6) Audit logging: Every lifecycle event (create, rotate, revoke, expire, escrow-read, escrow-purge) emits a structured event to the audit pipeline containing: actor, actor_type, actor_id_hash, source_ip, user_agent, old_key_fingerprint, new_key_fingerprint, scope, reason, correlation_id, k8s_pod (if applicable), and host_region. Events must be queryable in Console and streamed to customer audit sinks for Private deployments.

Private/Dedicated notes:
- Private: KMS integration is customer-managed. If KMS is unavailable for escrow wrapping, rotation falls back to 'reference-only' rotation (metadata rotates, but key material must be replaced manually) and the UI surfaces an action to upload new key material. This path is documented and gated behind a feature flag.
- Dedicated: Cross-region propagation needs the dedicated control-plane to forward rotation events to region controllers. We'll reuse the existing replication channel from ENG-56440.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- A background migration will tag existing keys with owner/scope where determinable and mark untaggable keys as 'requires-admin-intervention'. We'll provide a 'bulk-tagging' UI and CLI helper.
- Old rotations prior to rollout will be importable to escrow with a 'retrospective-archive' flow if admin supplies original key material (rare).

Risk/edge cases:
- Loss of KMS access in Private may prevent escrow; mitigated by runbook and manual import flow.
- Delegation token theft: single-use tokens, very short TTLs (default 10m), and rotation events include source IP and UA for anomaly detection.
- Large customers with thousands of keys: background jobs will be rate-limited and sharded by org_id; migration can be scheduled per-org.

Open questions:
- Default retention window for regulated customers (should we offer 7 years via support ticket?).
- UI affordances for delegating rotation to CI/CD pipelines (one-click approve vs policy-as-code).

Deliverables:
- Rotation API, delegation token service, escrow store, metadata enforcement, migration job, Console changes (key detail + rotate button + delegation UI), telemetry and audit forwarding, runbook for emergency revoke.
acceptance_criteria: Rotation API implemented and returns new key metadata + rotation epoch
Delegation token flow: mint -> consume (single-use) -> audit event emitted
Escrow store contains KMS-wrapped old key material and retention metadata after rotation
Naming template enforced for all newly created keys; migration job surfacing exceptions
Structured audit events available in Console and exported to customer audit sinks for Private deployments
Automated tests cover rotation, delegation token misuse (replay), and escrow purge
Runbook published with emergency mass-revoke steps and cross-region propagation verified in Dedicated staging
migration_plan: Phase 1: Deploy backend APIs to staging and run end-to-end tests with mock KMS (2 weeks)
Phase 2: Run migration job for a small pilot org and surface exceptions in Console (1 week)
Phase 3: Gradual rollout to Hosted customers with opt-in for first 30 days, collect metrics
Phase 4: Enable for Dedicated customers after replication sanity checks; for Private, enable feature flag and document KMS requirements
Phase 5: Post-rollout hardening: reduce delegation token TTL, enable anomaly detection alerts
rollout_plan: Canary: 5% of orgs on Hosted use new rotation endpoints; monitor error rate and audit events
Beta: 25% with opt-in and early access for enterprise customers (support-guided)
GA: Default on for new keys; existing keys remain until migrated or admin-rotated
Console: UI changes behind feature flag; gradual exposure after backend is stable
